candidates.angle: अहङ्कार, ego, is named as a fault to be absent
वैराग्यम्, dispassion, is set against इन्द्रियार्थेषु, sense objects
दुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्, seeing the fault of suffering, is a repeated action

angle_en: Freedom begins when desire stops dressing suffering as reward.

en.intro: Krishna names one inner obstacle to clear sight, and then asks the listener to notice how he describes the endless cycle of bodily decline.
en.notice: Notice how the word ahankara, ego, appears right beside the list of birth, death, old age, and disease, and how Krishna names the seeing of these faults as a repeated act.
en.next: Krishna now moves to the next step, asking the listener to let go of attachment to people and places.
en.angle_en: Ahankara, ego, listed beside the cycle of suffering
en.meaning: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease.

hi.intro: कृष्ण एक आंतरिक बाधा का नाम लेते हैं, और फिर श्रोता को यह सुनने के लिए कहते हैं कि वे शरीर के निरंतर पतन को कैसे बताते हैं।
hi.meaning: इन्द्रियों के विषयों में वैराग्य, अहंकार का न होना, और जन्म, मृत्यु, बुढ़ापा तथा बीमारियों में दुख रूप दोषों को बार-बार देखना।
hi.notice: ध्यान दें कि कैसे अहङ्कार, यानी अहंकार, जन्म, मृत्यु, बुढ़ापे और बीमारियों की सूची के ठीक बगल में रखा गया है, और कृष्ण ने इन दोषों को बार-बार देखने की बात कही है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब अगले चरण पर जाते हैं, और श्रोता से कहते हैं कि वे पुत्र, पत्नी, घर और ऐसी ही अन्य चीज़ों के प्रति आसक्ति को छोड़ दें।
hi.angle_hi: अहङ्कार: अहंकार को जन्म, मृत्यु और बीमारियों की सूची के ठीक बगल में रखा गया है

en.intro: Krishna names one inner obstacle to clear sight, and then asks the listener to notice how he describes the endless cycle of bodily decline.
en.body: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease. Notice how the word ahankara, ego, appears right beside the list of birth, death, old age, and disease, and how Krishna names the seeing of these faults as a repeated act. Krishna now moves to the next step, asking the listener to let go of attachment to people and places.

issues: unsupported: "Notice how the word ahankara, ego, sits right next to the list of birth, death, old age, and disease, as if the root of all suffering is the false sense that 'I' am the body." (The source verse simply lists 'absence of ego' (अहङ्कारः एव च) alongside 'constant seeing of the fault' (दोषानुदर्शनम्) in birth, death, etc. It does not state or imply that the root of all suffering is the false sense of 'I am the body' (which is more characteristic of later Advaita interpretations). This is an unsupported factual/philosophical claim.)
